title: Placebo

source.name: Wikipedia — Placebo
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: A placebo ( pluh-SEE-boh) is a medicine or treatment intended to appear genuine to its recipient, but which has no pharmaceutical effect. Common placebos include inert tablets (like sugar pills), inert injections (like saline), sham surgery, and other procedures.

Placebos are used in randomized clinical trials to test the efficacy of medical treatments. In a placebo-controlled trial, any change in the control group is known as the placebo response, and the difference between this and the result of no treatment is the placebo effect. Placebos in clinical trials should ideally be indistinguishable from so-called verum treatments under investigation, except for the latter's particular hypothesized medicinal effect. This is to shield test participants (with their consent) from knowing who is getting the placebo and who is getting the treatment under test, as patients' and clinicians' expectations of efficacy can influence results.

The idea of a "placebo effect" was discussed in 18th century psychology, but became more prominent in the 20th century. Modern studies find that placebos can affect some outcomes such as pain and nausea, but otherwise do not generally have important clinical effects. Improvements that patients experience after being treated with a placebo can also be due to unrelated factors, such as regression to the mean (a statistical effect where an unusually high or low measurement is likely to be followed by a less extreme one). The use of placebos in clinical medicine raises ethical concerns, especially if they are disguised as an active treatment, as this introduces dishonesty into the doctor–patient relationship and bypasses informed consent.

Placebos are also popular because they can sometimes produce relief through psychological mechanisms (a phenomenon known as the "placebo effect"). They can affect how patients perceive their condition and encourage the body's chemical processes for relieving pain and a few other symptoms, but have no impact on the disease itself.

The placebo effect is a well-documented phenomenon, though it remains widely misunderstood and surrounded by misconceptions. Several studies have questioned its clinical relevance, fueling ongoing debate about its actual effectiveness. A 2001 meta-analysis of the placebo effect looked at trials in 40 different medical conditions, and concluded the only one where it had been shown to have a significant effect was for pain. Another Cochrane review in 2010 suggested that placebo effects are apparent only in subjective, continuous measures, and in the treatment of pain and related conditions. The review found that placebos do not appear to affect the actual diseases, or outcomes that are not dependent on a patient's perception. The authors, Asbjørn Hróbjartsson and Peter C. Gøtzsche, concluded that their study "did not find that placebo interventions have important clinical effects in general." This interpretation has been subject to criticism, particularly due to concerns about the adequacy of the methodology used. Recent research has linked placebo interventions to improved motor functions in patients with Parkinson's disease. Other objective outcomes affected by placebos include immune and endocrine parameters, end-organ functions regulated by the autonomic nervous system,, sport performance , and cognitive performance.

questions.q: Why should a placebo look the same as the real treatment in a clinical trial?
options: So that the real medicine can be tested on fewer people than usual
Then nobody knows who gets what, so expectations cannot influence the results
So that doctors can make sure that every patient is given the same dose
So that patients feel more comfortable when they take the medicine
questions.explain: Đoạn 2: giả dược nên không thể phân biệt với thuốc thật “to shield test participants… from knowing” vì kì vọng của bệnh nhân và bác sĩ có thể ảnh hưởng kết quả.

questions.q: What does “regression to the mean” help to explain?
options: Why patients in a control group can never show any change in their condition
Why doctors must always give the smallest dose of any medicine to patients
Why a patient may seem better when an extreme reading just becomes less extreme
Why a placebo works only when the patient fully understands the treatment
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: “regression to the mean” – một số đo cao/thấp bất thường thường được theo sau bởi số đo bớt cực đoan, nên cải thiện có thể không liên quan đến giả dược.

questions.q: What ethical problem arises when a placebo is presented as a real treatment?
options: The patient could become dependent on the tablets for life
The patient is deceived and so cannot give informed consent
The patient might refuse to take part in any future trial
The patient may have to pay a higher price for the medicine
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: dùng giả dược như thuốc thật “introduces dishonesty into the doctor–patient relationship and bypasses informed consent”.

questions.q: According to the text, what can a placebo mainly influence?
options: The speed at which a serious disease spreads through the body
The cure of illnesses such as Parkinson’s disease in most patients
How patients experience symptoms such as pain, rather than the illness itself
The results of blood tests that no patient can notice
questions.explain: Đoạn 4–5: giả dược ảnh hưởng đến cảm nhận và giảm đau/triệu chứng, nhưng “have no impact on the disease itself”.

questions.q: How does the writer present the conclusion of the 2010 Cochrane review?
options: As a result that came from a study of only one medical condition
As a key finding, though one criticised for the way the study was done
As an idea that every researcher in the field has agreed with fully
As final proof that placebos can never have any effect on any patient
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: các tác giả kết luận không thấy tác dụng lâm sàng quan trọng nói chung, nhưng cách giải thích này “has been subject to criticism” vì phương pháp.

questions.q: What does the final sentence of the text add to the discussion?
options: It proves that the 2001 analysis was wrong about the effect on pain
Newer work suggests placebos may influence some measurable outcomes too
It confirms that placebos only affect conditions related to pain
It shows that placebos are dangerous for people with certain diseases
questions.explain: Đoạn 5 (cuối): nghiên cứu gần đây liên hệ giả dược với cải thiện chức năng vận động ở bệnh Parkinson và các kết quả khách quan khác (miễn dịch, nội tiết, thể thao, nhận thức).

questions.q: A 2001 analysis found a significant placebo effect in only one of the conditions it examined.
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: phân tích gộp năm 2001 xét 40 bệnh và kết luận chỉ có đau là chứng minh được tác dụng đáng kể.

questions.q: Placebos are more effective when the patient believes they are expensive.
questions.explain: Bài không nói gì về giá cả hay niềm tin của bệnh nhân về giá của giả dược.
